text: We built an AI that can draft a week of social posts in about 90 seconds. Then we made it impossible for that AI to publish anything on its own. That was the hardest product decision we have made at Podosphere. The pitch everyone wants is 'AI that posts for you'. We think that is the wrong promise. Your brand voice, your client's reputation and your ad budget are not things you hand to a model and walk away from. So Podo Social works like this: Podo AI drafts the calendar, captions, replies and ad suggestions. Everything lands in one approval queue. You approve with one click, or edit, or reject. Only then does it go live. The AI does the 80% that is grind. You keep the 20% that is judgment. We now run Podosphere's own channels this way, in public. Every post you see from us went through that queue. Agency owners: how much of your week goes into drafting versus deciding?

Every time Meta changes reach, agencies panic for a week and then post exactly like before. The fix was never the algorithm. Post what your audience saves and shares, watch your own numbers instead of the news, and keep the cadence. What changed in your reach this month?

The case against fully autonomous marketing, in four lines. 1. A model does not know which client is nervous this week. 2. A model does not know the ad budget just got cut on a call. 3. A model does not carry the reputation when a post lands badly. 4. A model is brilliant at the draft and blind to the context. So we split the job. Podo AI drafts the posts, labels the inbox, scores the leads and flags the fatigued ad set. A human approves each one in a single queue, in about ten minutes a day. 80% of the grind gone. 100% of the judgment kept. That is not a limitation we apologise for. It is the product. If you run an agency, where would you draw that line?

Small business owners: you do not need 25 ideas a week. You need 3 strong ones and a way to reuse each of them. One long video becomes three short clips, one carousel, two text posts and a story. That is a full week from one afternoon of work. We are running Podosphere's own pages exactly this way, and every post is approved by a human before it goes out. Honest question for people who manage social for clients: what is the one task you would hand to an AI tomorrow, and the one you would never hand over? We are building around that line, so the answers matter.
